behaviour: Tofu set whole in its own carton or mould, with the curds neither cut nor pressed, so it keeps all its water and stays smooth, quivering and close to a custard. Firm tofu is made of curds that are broken up and pressed into a block, which is why it can be cut, pressed and fried. Silken tofu cannot take pressing or hard frying and falls apart in a pan that is stirred. It is slid into hot soup at the end, blended into a sauce or a dressing, or eaten cold with a sauce poured over.

contains.basis: It is made of soy milk.

stands_in_for.caveat: Silken tofu has not been pressed and breaks up in the pan, so it cannot be cut, pressed or browned.
Silken tofu has no fried skin and falls apart in a simmering broth, so it does not soak up the liquid the same way.
It is much softer and holds no shape under pressing or stirring, so slide it in gently at the end.
